description: How a request moves through the harness, from a person asking for something to a reviewed change and what the harness learns from it.

nodes.title: Human
nodes.summary: The person who wants something changed and who remains accountable for the result.
nodes.why: An agent has no stake in the outcome. Direction and acceptance stay with a person.
responsibilities: State the requirement and the constraints that matter.
Approve high-impact actions.
Accept or reject the finished change.
inputs: A need, a defect report, or a question about the system.

nodes.title: Request
nodes.summary: The requirement as written down, before any interpretation.
nodes.why: Keeping the original wording separate from the plan makes it possible to check later whether the delivered change is what was actually asked for.
responsibilities: Carry the requirement without reinterpreting it.
outputs: A requirement the harness can load context against.

nodes.title: AX Harness Core
nodes.summary: The vendor-neutral layer that loads context, decides what is permitted, and sequences the work.
nodes.why: The reusable parts belong in one place that depends on no particular stack and no particular vendor.
responsibilities: Resolve the project declaration against its profile.
Assemble the context a role needs.
Apply the lifecycle and the capability policy.
inputs: The project declaration and its profile.
outputs: A resolved configuration and the context, policy and lifecycle that govern the work.

nodes.title: Context
nodes.summary: The instructions, architecture notes and code a role needs in order to work from evidence.
nodes.why: An agent without the project's own context invents conventions instead of following them.
responsibilities: Resolve declared context references and verify they stay inside the project.
Provide the profile's architecture assumptions to whoever is working.
outputs: Verified references and the assumptions a change must preserve.

nodes.title: Workflow
nodes.summary: The lifecycle states a task moves through and the transitions that are permitted between them.
nodes.why: Narrow transitions stop a task reaching review without having been verified, and bound how often a failure can be retried.
responsibilities: Permit only declared transitions.
Return a failure to the state that can fix it.
Bound retries by the project's declared limit.
inputs: The current state and the retry budget.
outputs: The permitted next states, or a stop.

nodes.title: Policy
nodes.summary: The capability vocabulary that says what each role may do, and what nobody may do.
nodes.why: Controlled capability is the point. Reads are broad, writes are narrow and reviewed, and the high-impact actions belong to people.
responsibilities: Define the capabilities a role may hold.
Deny database writes, default-branch pushes, force pushes, deployment and secrets to every role.
Mark the actions that require human approval.
outputs: What the definitions say is permitted. Enforcement is not implemented.

nodes.title: Planner
nodes.summary: The role that turns findings into a bounded, ordered, verifiable plan.
nodes.why: Deciding scope before editing is what keeps a change reviewable and stops unrelated work creeping in.
responsibilities: Own scope, including what is explicitly out of scope.
Sequence work so each step can be verified alone.
Decide which roles the work actually needs.
outputs: An ordered plan with per-step verification and approval points.

nodes.title: Backend Engineer
nodes.summary: The role that implements server-side changes and the tests that cover them.
nodes.why: Implementation and its tests belong to the same owner, so behaviour and evidence arrive together.
responsibilities: Implement the planned backend change on a branch.
Keep controller, service and data-access responsibilities separated.
Report real gate outcomes, including failures.
inputs: An approved plan and a working branch.
outputs: A changed-file list, tests, and verification results.

nodes.title: Frontend Engineer
nodes.summary: The role that implements client-side changes, keeping them typed, accessible and responsive.
nodes.why: Accessibility and responsive behaviour are cheap while the change is being written and expensive to retrofit.
responsibilities: Implement the planned frontend change on a branch.
Own the server and client component boundary for that code.
Adapt to the API contract rather than changing it unilaterally.
inputs: An approved plan and the API contract.
outputs: A changed-file list, tests, and verification results.

nodes.title: Specialist reviewers
nodes.summary: The database, security, QA and integration roles, none of which may edit the code they judge.
nodes.why: A reviewer who can quietly fix what they find stops being a reviewer. Separating judgement from editing is what makes the verdict worth having.
responsibilities: Judge schema, security, gate results and cross-layer agreement.
Report findings rather than repairing them.
Escalate anything that needs a human decision.
inputs: A diff, the gate results, and the relevant contracts.
outputs: Findings ordered by severity, and an explicit verdict.

nodes.title: MCP and tools
nodes.summary: The interface through which a role reaches anything outside its own reasoning.
nodes.why: MCP is a connection standard, not business logic. Keeping capability behind one interface is what makes it possible to bound it at all.
responsibilities: Expose the codebase, documentation, repository metadata and database metadata.
Carry out only what the policy permits for the calling role.
Leave a record of what was reached.
inputs: A capability request from a role.
outputs: The result of a permitted operation. Not implemented: no connection exists yet.

nodes.title: Project
nodes.summary: The repository being changed, with its own declaration, profile and commands.
nodes.why: The harness holds no project-specific settings. Everything particular to a codebase lives with that codebase.
responsibilities: Declare its profile, context, commands, tools, permissions, gates and limits.
Own the commands that its gates actually run.
outputs: A working tree whose gates can be planned and run.

nodes.title: Quality gates
nodes.summary: The ordered checks a change must pass, each reporting passed, failed, unavailable or unrun.
nodes.why: A gate nobody could run and a gate nobody did run have not passed. Keeping those distinct is what stops a pipeline flattering itself.
responsibilities: Plan the applicable gates for the resolved project.
Keep passed, failed, unavailable and unrun distinct.
Refuse to report success for a pipeline that gates nothing.
inputs: A resolved configuration and a change.
outputs: A per-gate outcome with its evidence.

nodes.title: Evals
nodes.summary: Assessment of how the agent worked, which application tests cannot measure.
nodes.why: Tests say whether the software is right. They say nothing about whether the agent found the correct owner, preserved the rules, or stayed inside its permissions.
responsibilities: Score behaviour against declared expectations.
Treat a missing criterion as zero rather than ignoring it.
Fail outright on forbidden behaviour, however high the score.
inputs: The task, the diff, and the observed behaviour.
outputs: A weighted score and a pass or fail. No evaluation has been run.

nodes.title: Human review
nodes.summary: A person deciding whether the change should exist, not merely whether it compiles.
nodes.why: Gates and evals narrow what reaches a person. They do not replace the judgement about whether this was the right change.
responsibilities: Accept or reject the change.
Approve the high-impact actions policy reserves for a human.
inputs: The change, the gate outcomes, and the eval result.
outputs: Approval, or a rejection that returns to planning.

nodes.title: Pull request
nodes.summary: The proposal others review, and the record of what was decided.
nodes.why: Changes reach the default branch through review. Nothing in the harness may push there directly.
responsibilities: Carry the change, its rationale and its evidence.
Collect continuous integration results.
inputs: An approved change on a branch.
outputs: A reviewed change, and what the harness should learn from it.
